$comment: Source for the Playground demo page. Run `npm run playground:build` after editing; it inlines this file and demo-content.php into every demo blueprint. src/playground-demo.test.js checks that each sample reaches the parser backend named by its `format`, and that each example's `exports` match what the editor computes for Cite / Export.
title: Borges Bibliography Builder demo

sampleGroups.title: DOIs
sampleGroups.description: A bare DOI, a doi: prefix, or a doi.org link. Metadata comes from Crossref.

sampleGroups.title: PubMed and PubMed Central
sampleGroups.description: A PMID needs its PMID: label. A PMCID starts with PMC, with or without a PMCID: label.

sampleGroups.title: arXiv
sampleGroups.description: An arXiv: ID (modern or legacy), an arxiv.org link, or an arXiv DOI.

sampleGroups.title: ISBNs
sampleGroups.description: A labeled ISBN-13 or ISBN-10, or a bare ISBN-13 starting with 978 or 979. Books come from Open Library, with Google Books as a fallback.

sampleGroups.title: Library catalogs and the Internet Archive
sampleGroups.description: An OCLC number or LCCN needs its label (or its WorldCat or lccn.loc.gov link); an Open Library edition ID (OL…M) works on its own. An archive.org item link, ia: identifier, or ARK cites the edition the item names and keeps the archive.org page as the link. Records come from Open Library and the Internet Archive.

sampleGroups.title: BibTeX and BibLaTeX
sampleGroups.description: Whole entries, one or many. BibLaTeX fields such as date and location are understood.

sampleGroups.title: RIS
sampleGroups.description: Records exported from Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote, or another reference manager, one or many. Each record runs from TY - to ER -.

features: Citation Style (block sidebar): nine styles, Chicago Notes-Bibliography and Author-Date, APA 7, MLA 9, Harvard, IEEE, Vancouver, OSCOLA, and ABNT. Section 3 has an example of each. Switching reformats the generated text and keeps your manual edits.
Heading: type the heading in the block, and choose its level in the sidebar: Paragraph (the default, styled text) or H2 to H6. Leave it empty for no heading.

Edit fields: click any citation to correct its authors, title, year, DOI, and other fields; only the fields you change are saved. The pencil edits the displayed text instead, and Reset edits restores the generated text.
Manual Entry: next to Paste / Import, add a citation field by field when there is nothing to paste.
Duplicates: paste a DOI that is already in the list; it is skipped, not added twice.
Order: notes and author-date styles sort alphabetically. Numeric styles (IEEE, Vancouver) keep your order; use Move citation up/down.
Exports (block toolbar): copy the bibliography as text, or download BibTeX, BibLaTeX, RIS, or CSL-JSON.
Per-entry Cite / Export (sidebar, off by default): gives readers copy and download links under each entry on the published page. The Chicago Notes-Bibliography example in section 3 has it on.
Machine-readable output (sidebar): JSON-LD for search engines (on by default), COinS for Zotero, and embedded CSL-JSON. The examples in section 3 show each on and off.
Block settings: like other blocks, a bibliography takes an HTML anchor and extra CSS classes (Advanced), a font size, and top and bottom margin and padding.
Front end: use View Post to see the published bibliography, then open its read-only REST data.

examples.title: Chicago Notes-Bibliography: per-entry Cite / Export
examples.description: A book, a chapter, a journal article, and a webpage, sorted alphabetically. View the published page and open Cite / Export under any entry to copy it or download it as RIS, BibTeX, BibLaTeX, or CSL-JSON. Settings: Per-entry Cite / Export on, and every machine-readable layer on (JSON-LD, COinS, embedded CSL-JSON); heading Works Cited at level H4.
